task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: primary play types of absent player
methodological_questions: Can the closest pre-absence initiation-profile teammate be identified as the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
How many absence spells across how many distinct absent players are needed to test this?
Do play-type gains after absence reflect reorganization, or regression to the mean and sample-size noise?
How should similarity between teammates be defined and validated, and does the answer depend on that definition?

historical_evidence.finding: Tested whether an elite creator's signature action raises teammate PPP over the next k possessions with the same lineup. All creators were horizon=0. Jokic lag-1 ATT=+0.0282, CI[-0.043,+0.099], p=0.3779, recorded as a clean null. Secondary result: Antetokounmpo +0.075 distinct initiators over the next 3 possessions (perm p=0.0002, BH 0.003), with the structure recorded as not effective. Failure mechanism recorded as B_powered_null. Samples were n=1880 (Jokic), 1804 (Giannis), 325 (Doncic). Validation status recorded as NOT_RECORDED.

Connector absence versus usage-matched non-organizer absence. Connector absence displaced team offensive identity (D_A) more than role-matched absence: unmatched 0.2020 vs 0.1021, t=5.97, p=2.87e-08. Usage-matched paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, t=6.35, p=7.35e-09, n=96. Versus terminal: +0.0777, t=2.37, p=0.0261, n=25. Limited by [prior work]; risks recorded as MECHANICAL_FLOOR and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER. Built on 908 player-seasons.

Case studies on alignment of team mix with an engine recommendation versus ORtg. Closest versus most-deviated tercile +3.3 ORtg adjusted (raw +5.2); Spearman rho >0.4 in 62% of games. No CI or test reported for +3.3. Limited by [prior work]; risks recorded as BASE_RATE and LABEL_ERROR. The in-game PT ranking used as the rho target shares outcome data. Mechanism recorded as E_unclear.

Sequential same-player and teammate X->Y play-type premiums in PPP above baseline. Examples: P. George DRIVE->SPOT_UP +0.560 (n=31, t=+2.2); K. Towns->O. Anunoby DRIVE->SPOT_UP +0.398 (n=30). Most cells recorded as DIRECT. Limited by [prior work] and [prior work]. Mechanism recorded as E_unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing whether an elite creator's absence-adjacent or signature-action presence lifts lineup-matched teammate PPP at lags 1-3.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null): no creator produced a positive lineup-matched teammate-PPP lift at any lag. Validation was not recorded. The one positive secondary result (distinct initiators) was recorded as not an effective structure.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using engine-mix alignment ranking as the target for a rho-based test of ORtg gains.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear with [prior work]. The rho target used in-game PT ranking, which shares outcome data. No CI or test was reported for the headline +3.3. Three of six cases were labelled honest counter-examples.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking teammate and same-player play-type sequence premiums to identify top gainers.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear with [prior work] and [prior work]. Top cells have small n (30-62). Most cells were recorded as DIRECT, so they are not a test of reorganization.

evidence_establishes: Earlier work by this project has tested teammate-level responses to a star's presence or absence using play-by-play and lineup-matched designs, and at least one such design returned an adequately powered null.
Usage-matched comparisons against non-organizer absences are a design that has been used in this project, with n=96 matched pairs and a recorded supported result (SF-[prior work]).

Ranking teammates by play-type premiums with small per-cell n has been flagged as unstable ([prior work]), and outcome-derived labels have been flagged as a leakage-type label problem (SF-[prior work]).
[prior work] state that the structure of the questions was often not effective or not validated.
evidence_does_not_establish: None of the retrieved records tests the question as posed: that the closest pre-absence initiation-profile teammate is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types.
No retrieved record reports the closest-profile similarity metric, its validation, or a comparison of the three alternative definitions (profile, minutes, initiations or same-position minutes).
No retrieved record gives an effect size or power estimate for absence-level redistribution with 11 distinct absent players.
The retrieved results do not show whether play-type gains after absence exceed regression to the mean.
own_inferences: The 148 spells are nested within 11 absent players. The effective sample for a player-level claim is about 11, which is far below what the earlier usage-matched design (n=96 pairs, 908 player-seasons) needed.

The 'closest profile' teammate will mechanically be a high-usage, high-minutes teammate, so profile similarity and minutes are confounded. Any 'largest gainer' result may simply reflect the MECHANICAL_FLOOR of more minutes.
Primary play types of the absent player are selected on pre-absence usage, so gains in those types are subject to regression to the mean, which is an RTM_SELECTION issue.
Play-type labels and possession credit are derived from the same play-by-play used to define gains, so the outcome is partly derived from the label (OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL).
uncertainties: [prior work] do not say how many of the 148 spells fall in the completed 2025-26 windows versus partial periods; only completed data should be used.
The exact definition of 'primary types' and 'initiation profile' is not given in the task statement or records.
No validation status is recorded for SF-[prior work] (NOT_RECORDED), so its null cannot be treated as validated.
[prior work] do not say whether earlier studies controlled for coaching or roster changes across 2022-26 seasons.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records do not answer the question, but they changed the plan in three ways. (1) The rejected gravity null (SF-[prior work]) and the failed sequence-premium ranking ([prior work]) show that teammate-gain rankings with small or outcome-linked samples are unreliable, so the design must pre-specify a non-outcome-derived similarity measure and a null comparison. (2) The usage-matched design in SF-[prior work] gives a precedent for matching controls, which the design below adopts. (3) The label-error and outcome-shared-target problems in SF-[prior work] mean profiles and targets must be fixed before any outcome is computed. Together these lead to do_not_proceed as a confirmatory test on the current 11 cases, with only a descriptive, pre-registered analysis left open.

blocking_constraints.text: 11 distinct absent players (148 nested spells) give very low power to detect a teammate-level gain difference, and the closest-profile ranking is a single-case comparison per player.
Absent players' primary play types are selected on pre-absence usage, so post-absence gains are expected to regress toward the mean.
Closest-profile teammates tend to have high minutes and usage, so they gain more in raw counts without any reorganization effect.
Play types and initiator credit come from the same play-by-play used to measure gains, so label and outcome are not independent.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests whether the closest pre-absence initiation-profile teammate is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types. The nearest records are a rejected teammate-PPP null (SF-[prior work]), a supported usage-matched connector-absence design (SF-[prior work]), an outcome-linked alignment study (SF-[prior work]), and a non-hypothesis-test play-type premium ranking ([prior work]). They inform design and risks but do not answer the question.

risks.text: 11 absent players is too few for a confirmatory test; spells within a player are not independent.
Many primary play types for an absent player will have few possessions per spell, making per-type gains noisy.
Play-type and initiation-profile measures from play-by-play may have low test-retest reliability across seasons.
Selecting primary types on pre-absence usage and then measuring gains will produce apparent gains by regression to the mean.
Initiator and play-type labels are derived from the outcome data, so the target and the feature share information.
Play-type classification from the play-by-play feed may misassign actions, as flagged in SF-[prior work] and [prior work].
Teammates with more minutes or initiations will show larger raw gains by construction; minutes must be controlled or normalised.
The chance that some teammate is the largest gainer is high; a top-1 rule needs a null of random ranking across teammates.
Absence often coincides with injury, rotation changes, coaching changes, or trades, all of which alter usage independently of the absence.
The question allows three definitions of 'closest' (profile, minutes, initiations or same-position minutes), inviting a forking-paths choice.
A placebo that matches on minutes alone may fail to separate the profile effect from the minutes effect.
The data span 2022-23 to 2025-26 with rule and roster changes; play-type frequencies may shift over time.
Derived play-type records come from a graph database built from play-by-play; ID mismatches or duplicate possession credit could produce spurious gains.

design.estimand: Among teammates of an absent player, the difference in change in possession share for the absent player's pre-absence primary play types between the closest-profile teammate and usage-matched non-closest teammates, relative to matched pre-absence windows. A descriptive version is acceptable if the confirmatory version is not feasible.
design.unit: Teammate-by-absence-spell pair, with absence spells nested within the absent player; player is the independent cluster.
design.sample: Only completed data: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular and playoff seasons, plus 2025-26 regular season after 2026-04-13 and 2025-26 playoffs after 2026-06-21. Exclude partial windows. Start from the 148 spells over 11 players; report how many survive the minimum-possession rule.
design.power: Not adequate for a confirmatory test with 11 clusters. Pre-register a minimum detectable effect and a minimum number of distinct absent players (for example, 30 or more) before analysis. If the cluster count cannot be raised, present results as descriptive only.
design.controls: Match controls on minutes, pre-absence usage, and lineup. Include the absent player's team, season, and coaching change indicators. Use a pre-absence trend control. Use an out-of-sample split for the closest-profile definition: define profile on the pre-absence window only, and never use the outcome window to define similarity.
design.falsification: (a) Placebo absences: pseudo-absence windows from games where the player was active, with the same teammate matching; the closest-profile advantage should disappear. (b) Permutation of the profile ranking among teammates within each absence. (c) Minutes-only ranking as a rival prediction: if minutes explain the gain as well as profile, the profile claim fails.
design.multiplicity: Fix profile similarity as the single primary definition. Report minutes and initiation-count rankings as secondary, with Benjamini-Hochberg control across secondary tests.
design.decision_rule: Confirm only if the primary closest-profile teammate's gain exceeds usage-matched controls and the permutation and minutes-only comparisons both reject, at the pre-registered alpha, with cluster-robust inference over absent players. Otherwise report a null or inconclusive result. Do not interpret a gain without placebo support as reorganization.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 through 2025-26 as listed, using only completed windows: 2025-26 regular season after 2026-04-13 and 2025-26 playoffs after 2026-06-21. Freeze the derived play-type graph version before analysis and record it.
